A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Bootstrap3D. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite changes to the title, formatting, and numbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original CLIP/FID benchmarks, ablations, human evaluations of MV-LLaVA, and GPT-4V comparisons of generated objects in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds CRM comparisons, InstantMesh reconstruction results, and a Shape-E fine-tuning experiment in Appendix A.7.

M1.justification: The data-generation pipeline, MV-LLaVA instruction tuning and filtering, and TTR procedure remain unchanged. The Shape-E experiment applies the existing captioning and quality-filtering approach to another generator without introducing a new curation algorithm.

E1.justification: Figure 6 adds targeted qualitative evaluation using stylized, out-of-domain Bootstrap3D-generated conditioning images, beyond the CAD-style PixArt inputs used in the retained quantitative image-to-multi-view benchmark. The underlying dataset sources and standard and real-user prompt suites remain unchanged.

E2.justification: CRM becomes an evaluated comparator in Table 1 and qualitative comparisons; v1 only cited it. The new Shape-E experiment compares against original Shape-E and its Cap3D-fine-tuned variant. Existing benchmark comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Added experiments use InstantMesh alongside GRM for reconstruction, fine-tune Shape-E on 250K filtered BS-Objaverse examples under a Cap3D-referenced protocol, and condition qualitative image-to-multi-view comparisons on Bootstrap3D outputs. The original training budgets, benchmark metrics, and sampling settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Figures 6 and 9 examine out-of-domain failures, blurring, and detailed prompt following through qualitative comparisons. The TTR, captioning, data-quantity, and vision-encoder ablations remain unchanged. One supplementary opera-house style example is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-seed averaging for CLIP evaluation and four seeds producing 440 objects per method for GPT-4V comparisons. v2 adds no uncertainty intervals, error bars, significance tests, or revised repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: New results extend the evidence to CRM benchmarking, InstantMesh reconstruction, and direct Shape-E generation, with additional qualitative comparisons. Table 11 newly reports FID values of 37.2, 35.5, and 35.3 for Shape-E, Cap3D, and the proposed fine-tuning, respectively. Shared numerical table entries remain unchanged; the additions concern new comparisons and configurations.

T1.justification: The Gaussian diffusion equations and mathematical description of TTR are unchanged. Calling terminal noise Gaussian instead of random clarifies the existing formulation; no new assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The title focuses more explicitly on multi-view diffusion, but the abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same substantive contributions: the synthetic-data pipeline with MV-LLaVA, TTR, and one million captioned multi-view examples, supporting improved quality and alignment with maintained consistency.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly explains reconstruction-based consistency assessment when ground-truth 3D objects are unavailable and interprets the Shape-E results as evidence of applicability to direct neural-field generation. Appendix A.2 expands the interpretation of out-of-domain behavior. The original reconstruction and quality-estimation limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.7 documents the new Shape-E experiment's 250K BS-Objaverse examples, quality threshold greater than 3, and reliance on Cap3D's protocol. Section 4.2 specifies conditioning inputs for the new qualitative comparison. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware, and project-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Shap-E and Tailor3D and extends discussion to applying curated captions to direct 3D generation. The related-work discussion is shortened in places, while the central positioning around data scarcity, caption quality, and synthetic training data remains.

P1.justification: The title changes, related-work and evaluation passages receive localized edits, and appendices A–G become subsections under a single Appendix A, with two added experimental sections. Most existing prose and the main argument's structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds overview and comparison Figures 1, 6, 9, and 21 plus Table 11; restructures Table 2 by reconstruction method; and combines selected panels from v1 Figures 4–5. The lotus example remains in the appendix, while the opera-house figure is removed. A new report template also reflows figures and tables throughout.

improvement.justification: The InstantMesh comparison makes validation less dependent on GRM, CRM strengthens baseline coverage, and the Shape-E experiment tests the usefulness of curated data for another generator family. Table 2 also distinguishes reconstruction settings more clearly. These are useful gains, although the added Shape-E protocol remains briefly specified and uncertainty reporting is unchanged.
